That wrapper is then stored via `data: { key }`, so the credential key shape changes and downstream code reading `credential.key` (e.g. googleCredentials.refresh_token) would break. The finding's line number is slightly off (97 vs ~92) but the mechanism is real and verifiable

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff changes `key` from `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (parsed data object) to `parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)`. The new helper returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (with `{ success, data, ... }`), not the parsed `data` itself, and this wrapper is then persisted via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. That would store the wrong shape in the credential `key` column. Other updated call sites treat the return value as a safeParse wrapper (checking `.success` / using `.data`), confirming this is unintended in GoogleCalendarService.
